I need to figure out if we should convert a dangling edge cell on a colored stripe to a "1". For instance, in demo row 1, the last three cells changed to "1" with stripe color 5 and background 3. I’m trying to identify any interrupted horizontal stripe endpoints. Also, in row 21, it seems we could see changes at the boundary where the stripe transitions. I wonder if the pattern holds across other rows as well.

**Analyzing background cell replacement**

I’m considering replacing the background cell immediately to the right of a horizontal line with "1" when the line ends within an interior. In demo row 1, the line extends 27 cells with the final column being background 3. In row 5, it spans the full 28 cells. In testing row 21, where the stripe ends at col 16, I’d set col 17’s background to "1." But I wonder why row 3, which is full width, lacks a marker. It seems markers appear only at the edge of horizontal bands.

**Exploring cell marking strategies**

I need to test if, after 17 colored cells, the 10 trailing gaps could lead to marking col 17 as "1". I could replace the background at the right endpoint of a stripe, but it gets tricky with full-width lines. In row 21, which is interrupted on the right, I should mark the next cell. I’ll have to submit a program that creates a function to find horizontal runs shorter than their width and change the cell immediately after to "1". For example, demo row 1 runs from columns 0-26, while row 5 is fully colored.
